title: Slide a high-chair tray in to fit a seated toddler manikin: hold the front release while pushing, and stop at the last position that doesn't touch it
instruction: A toddler manikin is buckled into the high chair and the tray is locked in its outermost position. Using the release button under the tray's front edge, slide the tray in to the closest of its four positions that does not touch the manikin, make sure both locking fingers have clicked in, and let go.
context: Fitting the tray to a buckled-in child happens at every meal. The Graco Made2Grow manual says to press the button on the front of the tray and push it toward the seat, and warns: do not force the tray against the child, and be sure both adjustment fingers are engaged in the armrest slots. The tray only moves while the release is held, and the right stopping point is set by the child, not by a named notch.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robots' left, z up from the floor. A fixed white high chair (proportioned after a Graco Made2Grow; not manufacturer CAD) faces the arms: seat top at z=560, seat 280 mm deep x 320 mm wide with its front edge at x=660, backrest up to z=1080, footrest at z=380, four splayed 28 mm square tube legs, grey seat pad. Two white armrest rails (32 mm wide, 30 mm tall, top at z=720, centred at y=+/-170, from x=460 to x=800) each have four locking slots (18 mm long along x, 8 mm deep) in their underside centred at x=620, 650, 680 and 710, with dark tick marks on the outer face above them. A white plastic tray (300 mm front to back x 440 mm wide, 12 mm plate, 20 mm rim with a 120 mm gap at the front centre, 0.65 kg, light-blue insert, an orange pointer on each side in line with its locking finger) rests on the rails through two underside channels (3 mm side clearance) and starts locked in position 1, its centre at x=520, y=0. Under its front edge is a blue release button (80 mm wide, sticking out 22 mm) on a one-piece 60 g release bail that pivots 43 mm under the plate: pushing the button up to its 6 degree stop lowers both 12 x 20 x 16 mm locking fingers 15 mm out of their slots; a return spring lifts them when let go. A rigid toddler manikin (12-18-month size; torso 170 mm wide x 120 mm deep, 150 mm head, thighs, shins, feet and arms modelled as capsules and spheres; pink onesie, skin-tone limbs) sits buckled in the seat with the front of its belly at x=750. Tray positions 1-4 put the tray centre at x=520, 550, 580 and 610, leaving 80, 50 and 20 mm between the tray's rear rim and its belly at positions 1-3; position 4 would need -10 mm, so the tray meets the manikin before reaching it. For a real trial, use a toddler-size manikin or weighted doll (about 80 cm tall, 9-12 kg), harnessed in the seat, and set it so a 20 mm spacer block just fits between its belly and the tray's rear rim with the tray locked in position 3; then return the tray to position 1. Two YAM arms stand on 750 mm pedestals at (0, +/-305, 750) with 75 mm grippers open. All parts start still. spec.py and scene.py give every dimension.
scoring: Read from the tray's side pointers against the armrest ticks and the locking fingers' height in their slots (in real trials: the pointer/tick alignment plus a light pull on the tray). A finger is locked in a slot when it is within 4 mm of the slot's centre along the rail and its top is at least 3 mm up inside the slot; both fingers must be locked in the same slot. 0.25 when the tray has moved at least 10 mm in from position 1; 0.5 when both fingers are locked in position 2 or 3; 1.0 when both fingers are locked in position 3, both grippers are at least 5 mm clear of the tray and its release bail, and the tray and bail stay under 10 mm/s and 2 deg/s for ten consecutive 20 Hz frames. If the tray, the release bail or a gripper ever comes within 1 mm of the manikin, the tray drops below z=600, the tray leaves the published workspace, or fixed scenery moves more than 3 mm, the trial scores 0 for good. Anything else, including doing nothing, scores 0.
reset_notes: Tray locked in position 1 with the release bail at rest; all velocities zero; cameras and counters restored.
fidelity: Full-size rigid chair, tray and manikin with real colliders: the release bail is a native revolute joint with a 6 degree stop and a return-spring drive, and the fingers, slots, channels and rails all hold by contact, so the tray moves only while the button is held up and locks only when both fingers physically rise into slots. Simplified: the geometry is proportioned after the Graco Made2Grow rather than taken from its CAD; the real tray's alternative release (two squeeze handles underneath) is omitted; the manikin is rigid and fixed (no soft tissue or movement), and touching it is judged by a 1 mm proximity threshold rather than force; plastic friction (0.35 static, 0.30 dynamic) and the spring rate are estimates without hardware calibration.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the tray never moved; the run stopped at step 1,088 of 1,200 when its request budget ran out); demo: 1.0 (full score at step 252)
